penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Configuring WebRTC NAT traversal, TURN/STUN relays, and firewall rules for a specific customer's self-hosted setup requires per-customer technical assessment and implementation work — not a one-size automated delivery.

rationale: The pain is real but infrequent — IT admins configure their video infrastructure once, not repeatedly — meaning this is a one-time setup problem, not a recurring subscription opportunity. The buyer (IT admin at a privacy-sensitive SMB) is identifiable but rarely pays for managed relay services when they can follow a tutorial; willingness to pay is weak. Delivering a working TURN/STUN relay configuration for a customer's specific network topology requires hands-on technical assessment per client, which the human-fulfillment penalty captures; total drops to 2.5 after penalties.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. If the idea were repositioned as a self-serve managed TURN/STUN relay (customer points their Jitsi/BigBlueButton instance at our relay server, paying monthly), the fulfillment penalty might not apply — but that becomes a commodity infrastructure product competing with Twilio TURN, Cloudflare Calls, and open-source coturn, with no defensible edge for a solo operator. A solo non-technical operator cannot realistically compete in infrastructure relay services or provide credible configuration consulting to regulated-industry IT teams.
notes: Total 2.5 is well below the 5.5 validate threshold. Fails on willingness_to_pay (3 < 5), operational_autonomy (5 < 7), and buyer_clarity (5 < 6) build gates — but the score doesn't reach validate regardless.
